summary.name: Elastic Observability in SRE and Incident Response
summary.one_liner: A blog post explaining how site reliability engineering and incident response work, and how Elastic Observability (Uptime, APM, Metrics, Logs, alerting, search) supports them.
use_cases: Setting up SLO-based alerts for availability, latency, errors and saturation
Investigating a production outage across hosts, containers and services
Tracing latency to slow database queries or code paths
Routing incident alerts to PagerDuty, Slack or Jira
Building shared dashboards and KPI views for leadership
summary.what_it_does: The page is a long-form explainer rather than a product page. It defines SRE concepts (SLA, SLO, SLI, and common indicators like availability, latency, errors and saturation) and the prevention, discovery and resolution stages of incident response. It describes how Elastic Observability covers these with Uptime checks, APM traces, infrastructure Metrics and Logs, plus alerts that trigger actions to channels such as PagerDuty, Slack or Jira. It also explains the Elastic Common Schema as a shared data model and gives three worked incident examples.
notable: Maps each SLI type to a specific Elastic Observability area: Uptime for availability, APM for latency and errors, Metrics for saturation, Logs for correctness
Describes the Elastic Common Schema (ECS), an open source data model for unifying traces, metrics and logs
Includes a suggested alert message template (title, severity, rationale, observed and desired state, context, links)
Walks through three incident examples: availability, latency and errors
caveats: Marketing-heavy article; it does not give pricing, plan details or setup steps
Examples are illustrative scenarios rather than documented product behavior
